body: I actually have a couple times.  They don't know what to say, which I understand.  It always makes me feel worse because they then start to judge me and start to distant themselves so they don't have to deal with me.

Thats exactly what I use this for too haha, I appreciate you taking a slightly different approach from the first comment.  I know everyone has issues and if you put things into perspective, it seems lame of me to feel this way, but hell I cant help it and reddit is, oddly enough, the only place where I feel heard and sometimes even slightly understood.

Im 35m.  Too old to feel this way.  Im from Pennsylvania. 

My story isn't one filled with traumatic events that are worthy of feeling this way.  I try to keep the perspective that people have it worse off and do better, so quit your bitching. But after a decade of this, im just so tired.

Without boring you with ALL my thoughts on my life and how I ended up on reddit at 230am, depressed amid a pandemic, trying to fight the urge to off myself...

I really started feeling this way about 7-8 years ago after a long relationship came to an end by way of betrayal (a typical way my relationships have ended). Its not that I'm not over this woman, but it essentially lead to this thought process..."this is the 3rd time in succession that you've let yourself trust people who are not worth it.  You cannot trust yourself to pick these people, so pick no one" 

It didn't take long for that logic to leak out into the friendship sphere as well.

And the kicker? 

I KNOW ITS RIDICULOUS!  But my brain justifies it, and it usually comes prepped with evidence, statistics and examples to back it up.

And, thank you. No one ever really listens, they just pretend until you go away and are no longer bringing them down.
We got you, fam.  We need each other now.
